# Compress responses
# Placement: fetch (vcl_fetch)
# Priority: 10
# The same rule as Fastly's "Generated by default compression policy".
#
# Fastly generates that rule after the fetch snippets, and "Doc cache age
# (fetch)" ends vcl_fetch with return(deliver) for most URLs (/, /libraries/,
# /static/css/, /doc/, 404s, ...), so the generated rule never runs for them.
# A lower priority number runs earlier, so this snippet sets beresp.gzip before
# any of those returns. beresp.gzip only changes how the body is stored and
# sent; whether and how long a response is cached is unchanged.
#
# The default compression policy stays enabled. For URLs that reach it, it
# repeats the same decision, which is harmless.
if ((beresp.status == 200 || beresp.status == 404) && !beresp.http.Content-Encoding && (beresp.http.content-type ~ "^(?:text/html|application/x-javascript|text/css|application/javascript|text/javascript|application/json|application/vnd\.ms-fontobject|application/x-font-opentype|application/x-font-truetype|application/x-font-ttf|application/xml|font/eot|font/opentype|font/otf|image/svg\+xml|image/vnd\.microsoft\.icon|text/plain|text/xml)\s*(?:$|;)" || req.url ~ "\.(?:css|js|html|eot|ico|otf|ttf|json|svg)(?:$|\?)" ) ) {

  # Keep compressed and uncompressed copies apart in the cache.
  if (!beresp.http.Vary ~ "Accept-Encoding") {
    if (beresp.http.Vary) {
      set beresp.http.Vary = beresp.http.Vary ", Accept-Encoding";
    } else {
      set beresp.http.Vary = "Accept-Encoding";
    }
  }

  # Fastly normalizes Accept-Encoding before vcl_recv, so a browser sending
  # "gzip, deflate, br, zstd" arrives here as "gzip".
  if (req.http.Accept-Encoding == "gzip") {
    set beresp.gzip = true;
  }
}
